subject: Clarification: default lifecycle for request vs. model outputs (exports & erasure)
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.co>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Support - Brightleaf <security@brightleaf.co>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify what gets kept by default — requests vs outputs

Hi Mina / Kim,

Quick follow-up from our pre-sales review: can you confirm the default lifecycle for the different artifacts Redwood keeps for a hosted account? Specifically we need to know:

- By default, how long are raw requests (user prompts / uploaded content) retained?
- How long are model-generated outputs (summaries, code, documents) retained?
- Do streaming tokens/logs count as persisted logs or are they ephemeral?
- If we request an export/erasure, what actually gets included/removed and how long until it’s fully purged (including backups)?

I'm attaching the small sample export format we use on our side — would be helpful to see what an export generated by Redwood includes (PII or hashed identifiers). We are in the EU region and are sensitive about residency and erase guarantees.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Data Protection Lead — Brightleaf

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what gets kept by default — requests vs outputs

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details and steps for an erasure/export. Attaching our internal retention matrix for quick reference.

Summary (hosted API, default settings):
- Raw requests (user prompts / uploaded content): retained by default for 30 days. These are used for debugging, system health, and feature analysis.
- Model-generated outputs (final responses): retained by default for 90 days. We keep outputs longer to support replay, troubleshooting regressions, and customer QA.
- Streaming tokens and ephemeral KV cache: treated as ephemeral session artifacts — not indexed into long-term logs. Streaming traces are kept only for the session window and generally expire within 2 hours unless explicitly flagged for debugging.

Residency / deletion propagation:
- For EU-region customers, records are stored in EU data stores. When an erasure request is processed, the primary copies are marked for deletion immediately and a tombstone is written. The tombstone triggers an asynchronous purge across replicas and snapshot backups. In normal cases physical purge from backups is completed within 30–90 days depending on backup cadence and legal hold status.

What an export contains:
- Exports include request metadata (timestamps, request id, route), the raw input text (unless the customer has requested input redaction), model outputs, and basic diagnostic metadata (latency, model version).
- We never include internal system PII in exports (operator IDs, internal hostnames are removed). If you need input redaction (PII removal) before export, we can run a redaction pass but that is a separate operational step.

How to request an immediate erasure vs scheduled retention change:
1) Submit a support ticket with subject line: "Data Erasure Request – Brightleaf – <customer-id>" and include the HubSpot deal id (DEAL-5721).
2) We will confirm scope (time window, routes, models) within 24 business hours.
3) For immediate erasure we mark primary copies and stop further indexing; exportable artifacts will reflect that change. A background purge will remove replicas and backups per the 30–90 day window described above.

Notes & exceptions:
- Dedicated / Private customers: If you're on a Private deployment, you control the persistence layer and can configure different retention defaults; Redwood's control plane will not retain customer data beyond what the deployment operator configures.
- Legal holds: if a legal hold is required, deletion will be paused and we will coordinate escalation.

I'll follow-up with the runbook link and a brief explanation of what is redacted by default.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Product Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightleaf.co>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what gets kept by default — requests vs outputs

Adding a few implementation-level clarifications from the infra side so Brightleaf can plan: 

- Streaming traces: we capture a lightweight trace that indicates start/stop and aggregate token counts. The full token stream is not persisted beyond the session unless the customer flags the session for debugging (customer-facing flag or support action).
- KV cache: per-session, stored in RAM and a short-lived cache layer; it is not written to object storage by default and will be dropped at session end (TTL ~2 hours).
- Backups & snapshots: automated backups are incremental and stored within the selected region. The purge window for backups is tied to backup retention cadence; we estimate the 30–90 day window depending on snapshot frequency.
- Export format compliance: our export will include original input text unless you request redaction. We can run a redaction job that removes emails, phone numbers and identity tokens prior to export for an extra fee or as part of an enterprise workflow.

If Brightleaf needs a tighter SLA on purge propagation (e.g., guarantee physical deletion within X days), that typically maps to a Dedicated reservation or a Private deployment with a custom legal addendum. Happy to sketch options.

-Kim
Staff Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
